elements.element: Mutual (both parties) right to assign to a successor
elements.evidence: "provided that either party may assign this Agreement to a successor"

elements.element: Assignment to successor conditioned only on written notice (no consent)
Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: clause only permits assignment "to a successor"; no affiliate carve-out

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: generic "successor" with no merger/acquisition/asset-sale enumeration, and the right is mutual rather than a Customer-side right

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not unreasonably withheld)
elements.evidence: "either party may assign this Agreement to a successor upon written notice" gives Contractor the same consent-free right

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: no competitor restriction appears in the clause

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: clause is silent on change of control; no termination right visible in this clause

reasons: The locked fallback level is fully satisfied: the added proviso creates a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, and the pre-existing "not unreasonably withheld" consent standard continues to govern all other assignments.

Preferred is not met (no affiliate carve-out, no asymmetry in Customer's favour, no competitor bar, no change-of-control protection), but that is acceptable given the locked fallback target and should be noted in the rationale rather than redlined further.

Edit is minimal: a single appended proviso rather than a clause rewrite; subcontracting and transfer restrictions and the consent standard remain intact, introducing no undefined terms or dangling mechanics.
